column1: # THE ERROR-CODE REGISTRY -- the shared contract for engine error codes.
# Every error code either implementation can attach to a failure is
# registered here with its CLASS. This file is the source of truth: both
# runners (ts/test/spec.test.ts, go/spec_test.go) execute each row below
# (mode `errcode`) against the engine's own code->class table
# (ts/src/hints.ts `codeClasses`, go/hints.go `codeClasses`), and each
# runner additionally asserts SET EQUALITY between this file and its
# engine table -- a code present in an engine but absent here (or the
# reverse) fails the suite in that engine.
# Columns: code<TAB>errcode<TAB>class<TAB>since
#   code  : the frozen snake_case code string (the NilVal `why`).
#           Codes are a CONTRACT: append-only, renames forbidden --
#           with ONE sanctioned exception, recorded in ADR-011: the
#           disjunction-empty pair was renamed `|:empty`/`|:empty-dist`
#           -> `empty`/`empty-dist` in 0.54.0, because the `|:` prefix
#           named a spelling the author may never have written (a bare
#           `*x` default refuses with it now), and a code that lies
#           about its own origin is worse than a frozen name. A rename
#           needs an ADR; nothing else does. A code
#           that ends in `:` or `[` is a dynamic-prefix family -- the
#           engine appends a name/value (e.g. `func:upper`, `ref[$.x]`)
#           and class lookup falls back to the longest registered prefix.
#   errcode : the spec mode (fixed).
#   class : one of conflict | incomplete | reference | parse | budget |
#           compat |
#           internal (see below). Classes drive report verdicts and exit
#           classes (docs/capability-review/g2-validation-verb.md), so a
#           class change is a breaking change.
#   since : the version line (TypeScript series) at which the code was
#           first REGISTERED. Codes predating the registry all carry the
#           registry's inception version, 0.51.0.
# THE CLASSES
#   conflict   : the source asks for something that can never hold --
#                two values with no common lower bound, a value refused
#                by a language rule, an impossible function argument.
#   incomplete : nothing contradicts, but residue remains -- a value the
#                truth requires has not been supplied yet.
#   reference  : a name or path that does not resolve.
#   parse      : the source text itself is malformed or unusable.
#   budget     : an evaluation bound was exceeded (cycles, passes,
#                nesting depth) -- see docs/capability-review/g5.
#   compat     : the subsumption query's report vocabulary (G3) -- the
#                compat_* findings and the sub_* undecided reasons.
#   internal   : the engine reached a state it should not reach.
# RULINGS the class column encodes (decided at registry inception):
#   - decimal_budget is class CONFLICT, not budget: the exactness budget
#     is a fixed language rule about the VALUE (4096 digits / scale
#     4096), not an evaluation resource -- no re-run with a larger
#     budget exists, so the repair action is "change the value", which
#     is what conflict means. The budget class is reserved for
#     evaluation bounds (cycles, passes, depth).
#   - lossy_integer_literal is class CONFLICT for the same reason: the
#     literal is well-formed but refused by a value rule; the repair is
#     writing the `0d` form.
#   - unknown_function is class REFERENCE: a name that fails to resolve,
#     exactly like an unresolved path or variable.
#   - The transient disjunct-trial sentinel `|:trial-nil`
#     (ts/src/val/NilVal.ts TRIAL_NIL) is deliberately NOT registered:
#     it never surfaces to user-visible output, and the engines assert
#     set equality, so registering it would claim otherwise.
# parse -- the source text is malformed or unusable
parse
syntax
parse_unknown
parse_bad_src
# A version-control conflict marker left in the source (issue #5).
# Without it `<<<<<<< HEAD` parsed as ordinary text and the document
# quietly became a list of strings.
merge_conflict
# An @"..." include refused by the trust profile's include capability
# (G5 phase 3, docs/trust.md): a path escaping the confinement root, or
# any include under the 'none' capability. Parse-stage, deterministic,
# and raised (never injected as a value) so a bare-member include cannot
# vanish in the merge.
include_denied
# An @"..." include whose EXTENSION is not one the engine reads as
# Aontu source (ADR-012, use-cases/BUGS.md §49). `.aon`, `.aontu`,
# `.json` and `.jsonld` parse; everything else -- and a name with no
# extension -- is refused by name rather than guessed at. Parse-stage
# and raised, not injected, for the same bare-member reason
# include_denied is.
include_extension
# A built-in called with the wrong number of arguments (issue #51).
# Arity is known for every built-in, so a surplus or missing argument is
# a mistake in the SOURCE and is refused where the author can see it.
func_arity
# A key or element written with no value (issue #48). An elision used to
# be a null, which made a mistake in the source indistinguishable from a
# deliberate `a:null`.
elided_value
unify_no_src
incomplete_expression
pref_implicit_bag
alias_not_toplevel
alias_in_path
not_number
negative
decimal_syntax
# conflict -- no common lower bound, or a value refused by a rule
# (constraint covers the whole algebra family: membership failure,
# empty meets at composition time, and domain/kind mixing -- one code,
# decided once at its introduction, since the registry is append-only.)
constraint
constraint_pattern
must
scalar_value
scalar_kind
no_scalar_unify
scalar-type
not-scalar-type
map
list
closed
literal_nil
nil_gen
unite
empty
empty-dist
pref_rank_clash
exact_float_mix
inexact_integer_sum
decimal_budget
pick_key
aggregate_data
aggregate_empty
join_member
divide_by_zero
inexact_divide
float_overflow
lossy_integer_literal
arg
invalid-arg
# THE SIGNATURE GATE (docs/design/SIGNATURES.0.md): a driven argument
# that does not fit the declared signature -- a wrong-kinded scalar, a
# container or a kind marker in a value slot whose type is scalar-kind
# words. The hint renders the signature line and names the argument.
# Class conflict for invalid-arg's reason: the VALUE is what is wrong,
# where func_arity's parse class says the CALL is.
func_arg
no_first_arg
key_level
func
func:
op
op:
op[
make
resolve
operate
close
# incomplete -- residue: the truth requires more than was supplied
no_gen
disjunct_no_gen
conjunct
mapval_no_gen
mapval_required
mapval_spread_required
listval_no_gen
listval_required
listval_spread_required
required_listelem
# reference -- a name or path that does not resolve
# (path_cycle is a PROVEN structural cycle -- a defect of the model,
# not a spent evaluation bound: raising a budget never fixes it, so it
# is class reference, not budget; G5's ruling.)
no_path
path_cycle
ref
ref[
var
var[
unknown_var
invalid_var_kind
unknown_function
multisource_not_found
# budget -- an evaluation bound was exceeded
unify_cycle
max_depth
budget_passes
# internal -- the engine reached a state it should not reach
internal
unify_no_res
unknown_op
# compat -- the subsumption query's report vocabulary (G3,
# docs/capability-review/g3-subsumption-evolution.md). These codes ride
# G2's finding object from the `subsume` and `breaking` surfaces; the
# `sub_*` codes are the UNDECIDED reasons, spec-pinned so the taxonomy
# cannot grow silently.
compat_narrowed
compat_required_added
compat_default_changed
compat_marks_changed
sub_unresolved
sub_disjunct_distribution
sub_path_dependent_spread
sub_evaluate_only
sub_default_indeterminate
# The deprecation mark's point-of-use warning (G3 phase 4,
# deprecate(x, m)): vet reports a deprecated value's use at severity
# `warning`, the slot G2 reserved for this mark; it is the one compat
# code that can appear in a vet report as well as a subsume/breaking
# one.
deprecated
# The default-validity lint (G3 phase 5): a disjunction's effective
# default is not an instance of any remaining alternative. Severity
# `warning` in vet for now — today's engine generates the bad default
# and existing documents may lean on it, so promoting the warning to an
# error is itself a breaking change, sequenced through the `breaking`
# gate.
pref_not_instance
# The overlay patch verb (G7 phase 5, `aontu set`): the assignment was
# not <path>=<value>. Class `parse` -- what is malformed is source
# text -- and report-layer, so no NilVal ever carries it.
patch_assignment
# `set --in-place` refusing to rewrite, as WARNINGS: the assignment
# still appends, so the run is no worse than it would have been and the
# verdict must not move. What they add is the reason, which is the whole
# value of asking for --in-place over plain set.
# `patch_not_editable` is class `reference` because it is a LOCATING
# failure -- the path names no single literal this overlay can edit,
# whether because the value comes from a spread or a ref, because the
# site names a compound's opening token rather than the whole value,
# because the literal is in an included file, or because it is a
# constraint rather than a pin. `patch_ambiguous` is the same class and
# split out because the remedy differs: two statements pin the path and
# the author must say which one they meant.
# `patch_span_mismatch` is class `internal` deliberately. Both the site
# and the text come from the same source this run just parsed, so a
# disagreement between them is a state the engine should not reach --
# and it is checked anyway, because the alternative to checking is
# writing over bytes nothing can account for.
patch_not_editable
patch_ambiguous
patch_span_mismatch
inverse_name
list_length
recursion_unexpanded
recursion_budget
# THE CHECKED LINK (G4 phase 2, `refer(t?)`). Two codes. `refer_address`
# is the value met being no address at all -- anything that is not a
# path value, bare strings included (ADR-016) -- class `parse`, because
# what is wrong is the text and no later pass can repair it. `refer_unresolved` is a well-formed
# address that names nothing in this evaluation -- class `reference`,
# the same class as `no_path`, because it is the same kind of miss.
# Integrity is a UNIFICATION-time property: within one evaluation the
# document-set is fixed, so the last pass decides, and the refusal is a
# located nil rather than a vet-time deferral. A `t` that cannot be
# unified into the target is NOT in this list: that is the ordinary
# conflict of whatever disagreed, which is what constraint flow means.
refer_address
refer_unresolved
# rel(t?) (RELATIONS.0.md P1): the relation constraint's own codes,
# carried by the same refer machinery underneath.
rel_address
rel_unresolved
# FIRST-CLASS PATHS (docs/design/PATHS.0.md). One code: text that is
# not a tree address, met by `path(p)`'s capture -- literal or computed
# argument alike (ADR-016). Class `parse` for refer_address's reason --
# what is wrong is the text, and no later pass can repair it. An
# address that names nothing is NOT a path error: a path value is
# data, and existence stays refer()'s contract.
path_address
# RELATION GRAPH CHECKS (G4 phase 5). Two report-layer codes, class
# `conflict`: the model contradicts a property it declared for itself.
# NEITHER is a NilVal code -- both are GLOBAL and NON-MONOTONE (an
# acyclic graph becomes cyclic when one more edge unifies in), so they
# are checked after unification and never by it. `aontu relations`
# reports them; the lattice never sees them.
relation_cycle
relation_inverse_missing
# THE GENERATION COMBINATORS (G8 phase 1, `pack` and `each`). Three
# codes, all class `parse`: what is wrong is the CALL as the author
# wrote it, and no later pass repairs it. `pack_data`/`each_data` is
# data with no children to generate from — a scalar, a kind, a
# residual. `pack_key` is a packed list element that is not a string:
# the elements of a packed list ARE the generated keys, and a key is a
# name. Keying by position instead would churn every generated child
# the moment the list was reordered, which is the Terraform `count`
# lesson the design names.
pack_data
pack_key
each_data
# SELECTION (G8 phase 2, `filter` and `match`). `filter_data` is class
# `parse` for the same reason `pack_data` is: the CALL names something
# with no children to select from. `match_none` is class `conflict` --
# the value and every pattern written for it disagreed, which is an
# ordinary failed meet, reported once for the whole form and naming
# the patterns that were tried.
filter_data
match_none
# THE PLACEHOLDER (G8 phase 3, `_`). One code, class `conflict`: two
# placeheld calls met and neither has a value to fill the other, so
# there is nothing to pick between them. A hole with a value on the
# other side is not an error at all -- it is the whole point.
place_pair
# MODULES (G6 phase 2). Three codes are class `parse`: a module import
# is resolved while the source is READ. `module_path` is a module path
# that is domain-shaped and carries a major -- so it ROUTES here -- but
# cannot legally be a directory on every platform: an empty element, an
# element beginning or ending with `.` (which is what forbids `..`), or
# a reserved device name. Refused before anything is built from it,
# because `pathJoin` CLEANS `..` rather than refusing it, and a store
# path built from one escapes the store.
# `module_missing` is a module in
# neither local store -- evaluation never touches the network, so
# fetching is a separate step and the message names it.
# `module_integrity` is a module that IS there and does not have the
# meaning it was pinned to; the pin is a canon-hash, so it survives
# formatting and breaks on meaning.
# `module_depth` is class `budget`: verification EVALUATES the module,
# that evaluation resolves the module's own imports, and a vendor tree
# that leads back to itself would recurse until the host ran out of
# stack -- a verdict that depends on the machine, which is what
# docs/trust.md forbids. The bound makes it a stated refusal, exactly
# as `unify_cycle` does for the same reason.
module_path
module_missing
module_integrity
module_depth
# THE TREE VIEW (`aontu view tree`, docs/design/VIEWS.0.md). A relation
# named to the view that has no edges in the document is refused rather
# than drawn empty: an empty tree and a misspelled name are the same
# file on disk. Class `reference` -- a name that does not resolve. A
# root that names no node of the drawn graph reuses `refer_unresolved`,
# the code every verb answers a path that names nothing with.
view_relation_unknown
view_kind_unknown
view_profile_unknown
view_rows_exceeded
view_line_break
view_relation_ambiguous
view_sets_shape
view_sets_required
view_at_required
view_group_required
